text:
Alex K: seeing a small but recurring tail-latency spike in eu-west around 03:10-03:25 UTC, looks correlated with a few tenants hitting high NVMe io_util. dedicated-pools aren't triggered but shared slices slow down
Maria P: can you paste the grafana panel or query?
Alex K: https://grafana.redwood/eu-west/d/gpu-latency?panelId=7 span=03:00-03:30 - you'll see egress bytes + iops jump, pcie latency +50ms, kv-cache miss rate up 2.5x
Jonathan L: saw some TCP retransmits in the same window from node-az3-rack12. NIC queue depth spiked. suspect noisy-io tenant + batch job fighting for DMA
Nisha (oncall): infra-bot fired an alert and auto-fallback routed ~8% of requests to the lower-capacity reserved pool which kept p99 but raised cost. do we want a different fallback for this pattern?
Alex K: yes, prefer shield->prefetch fallback rather than reserved-pool to avoid cost jump. also want a short-term mitigation: pin suspected tenant to soft-isolated slice for 10m and throttle its egress burst
Maria P: query I ran: `sum(rate(nvme/io_ops[1m])) by (tenant)` shows tenant:ml-batch-42 at 12k iops during the spike, others at ~1k
Jonathan L: if it's NVMe-heavy we can flip io_scheduling on that slice to deadline + cap bursts. quick change: `kubectl patch gpudriverconfig gpufarm -p '{"spec":{"ioBurstPct":30}}'` (dry-run first)
Nisha (oncall): infra-bot runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-neighbor-io - recommends: soft-isolate tenant, throttle egress, enable prefetch cache, consider routing to dedicated pool if >3 recurrences/day :pager:
infra-bot: ALERT 1789994444: egress_iops_high eu-west-3 - affected nodes: node-az3-rack12,node-az3-rack13. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/noisy-neighbor-io. suggested play: soft-isolate -> throttle -> monitor 15m -> escalate to dedicated fallback
sre_oncall: approved temporary soft-isolation for tenant ml-batch-42 from 03:18->03:40 UTC. applying throttle rule now. ping @Maria P for followup logs
Maria P: copying the kube patch I ran for telemetry: ```bash
kubectl -n infra annotate slice ml-batch-42 isolation=soft-isolated --overwrite
kubectl -n infra patch qospolicy ml-batch-42 -p '{"spec":{"egressBurstLimit":300}}'
```
Alex K: after the patch p99 dropped back to baseline in ~6m, nvme iops for ml-batch-42 fell to ~1.8k. cost delta if we had routed to dedicated pool would have been ~+18%/hour so glad we avoided that
Jonathan L: next steps: add rule in routing-engine to prefer prefetch-shielding policy for nvme-dominant signatures (iops>5k && kv_miss>1.5) and a blackhole window to avoid oscillation
Nisha (oncall): opened a ticket: RW-OPS-1428 to implement routing-engine rule + telemetry enrichment. tagging @eng-runtime for kernel-level knobs.
Alex K: awesome, thanks all. let's keep this thread for postmortem notes if it recurs. :thumbsup:
